title: Anthropic Is Now Public: Claude's Maker Opens at $111.50 on Nasdaq Under ANT, Raising $93.5 Billion
summary: Anthropic, the company behind Claude, began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19 under the ticker ANT. Shares were priced at $83 and opened at $111.50, according to Nasdaq. With the underwriters' extra shares, the offering raised about $93.5 billion, plus $26 billion from a concurrent private sale to chip and cloud partners.
body:
Anthropic, the company behind Claude, became a public company on November 19, 2026. Its Class A shares started trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT, a month after the company filed its S-1 with the SEC. According to Nasdaq, the stock opened at $111.50 per share. Co-founders Dario and Daniela Amodei marked the listing at the opening bell ceremony at Nasdaq MarketSite in New York.

The numbers

Anthropic priced the offering on November 18 at $83.00 per share: 980 million shares, of which about 956 million were sold by the company and about 23.6 million by existing stockholders. On November 20 the deal closed, and the underwriters bought all 147 million extra shares available to them, bringing the total to 1.127 billion shares.

Gross proceeds came to about $93.5 billion, of which about $91.6 billion went to Anthropic; the rest went to the selling stockholders. At the same time, Anthropic sold non-voting Class N shares at the same $83 price to AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, NVIDIA and TSMC Partners for about $26 billion. Together, the IPO and the private placement raised about $119.5 billion before fees.

Where the money goes, and who stays in control

In its final prospectus, Anthropic says it will use the money for general corporate purposes, including investments in compute and infrastructure and hiring. The company remains a public benefit corporation, legally required to balance shareholder returns with its stated mission of developing advanced AI "for the long-term benefit of humanity."

Control stays concentrated. An independent Long-Term Benefit Trust elects the directors who make up a majority of the board, and a single special share held by the seven co-founders carries 50.1% of the votes on most stockholder matters. Public ANT shareholders therefore have limited say over how the company is run.

What this means if you use Claude

Nothing changes in the product today. Anthropic has not announced any change to Claude plans, prices or limits in connection with the listing. Your Claude subscription, Claude Code and the API work as before.

More money for capacity. Most of the new capital is earmarked for compute, which is what sets usage limits and model speed, so it is worth watching whether limits loosen in the coming months. Keep in mind that a public company also reports to shareholders every quarter, and pricing decisions may follow. If you are choosing an assistant for your work, compare on the tasks you actually do, not on the company's market headlines: our ChatGPT vs Claude comparison is a good place to start. This article is news, not investment advice.
